October 2024 Welcome to the monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners. We are happy to share information on significant news and events in Ada County. Tom Dayley - Commissioner Rod Beck - Board Chairman Ryan Davidson - Commissioner ADA COUNTY JURY OFFICE RECEIVES NATIONAL RECOGNITION The more you know about jury duty in Ada County the more you realize what an honor and privilege it is to serve. When you’re called for jury service in Ada County, we value your time and we put you first. The Ada County Jury Office received national recognition on Friday October 18, 2024 for the multiple ways the office assists jurors who are selected for jury duty. The G. Thomas Munsterman Award for Jury Innovation is a prestigious award that emphasizes the need for jury offices to develop creative solutions and innovative approaches to make this important civic duty a positive experience for anyone who is selected. Pictured Left to Right: Chris Van Sickle - Deputy Jury Commissioner Jackie Mayorga - Deputy Jury Commissioner Randy Rutland - Ada County Jury Commissioner Natalya Bleier - Deputy Jury Commissioner October 2024 Pictured Left to Right: Sandra Barrios, Trial Court Administrator; Hon. Judge Steven Hippler; Ada County Clerk Trent Tripple; Randy Rutland, Ada County Jury Commissioner; Chris Van Sickle, Deputy Jury Commissioner; Paula Hannaford, Director, Center for Jury Studies NCSC; Jackie Mayorga, Deputy Jury Commissioner; and Natalya Bleier, Deputy Jury Commissioner

# Page 2^page=2
If you get picked for jury duty in Ada County, we’ll pay for your parking, provide Uber service to and from the Courthouse, provide meals, financial assistance with childcare and even offer counseling service. We do this because when someone is on trial, the right to have a jury of their peers decide their fate is one of the cornerstones of our entire system of government. Thank you to Ada County Jury Commissioner Randy Rutland and his delightful staff for setting such high standards and changing the way so many people view jury duty. If you’ve served on an Ada County jury – thank you! If you are selected, please know we’ll make the process as easy as possible. Ada County has hundreds of jury trials each year. We are humbled by the overwhelmingly positive feedback we receive from our jurors – many who call jury service one of the biggest learning experiences and honors of their lifetime. 2

ADA COUNTY CELEBRATES JAN BENNETTS DAY! Thirty years of exemplary public service recognized in October Ada County Commissioners signed a proclamation designating October 8, 2024 as Jan Bennetts Day. Our Ada County Prosecutor Jan Bennetts has served the citizens of Ada County since 1994. In recognition of her outstanding career in public service, Ada County Commissioners presented Bennetts with an Ada County flag and a signed proclamation. The Ada County Prosecutor’s Office which employs 184 people including 80 attorneys seeks justice in the prosecution of criminal cases and provides exceptional legal advice and guidance to Ada County elected officials and department heads. Thank you Jan Bennetts for setting a high standard for your office and serving the citizens of Ada County with distinction. HYLAND 2024 INNOVATION AWARD A project that helps our community’s youth and families Ada County IT and Ada County Juvenile Services have been awarded the Hyland 2024 Innovation Award. Hyland has an international business footprint and is one of the leading providers of content solutions. Ada County’s project beat out two other finalists: The Municipality of Querétaro, Mexico, and the University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center. The shared award for Environmental and Social Impact recognizes the Bridge Youth and Family Resource Center – an innovative and highly successful early intervention program to keep youth out of the juvenile justice and child welfare systems. Working together with Juvenile Services, Ada County IT created a customized solution that streamlines referrals, manages case data and enhances communication with stakeholders. The Bridge was previously selected as one of six centers from across the country to participate in the National Assessment Center Association’s “Assessment Center Outcome Reporting Network” or ACORN initiative. This initiative will help define measures to consistently report outcomes and performance indicators that align nationally across centers. Although the Bridge is a newly established resource center, it was chosen in the “advanced” data capacity category, primarily because of the Onbase case management system. 3

# Page 4^page=4
AWARD-WINNING PLANS FOR THE PARK AT EXPO IDAHO You’ve likely heard about The Park at Expo Idaho, and you’ll be hearing even more in the coming months and years. When completed in 2026 this 50-plus acre park will transform an area along the Boise River into a vibrant outdoor recreation area for everyone to enjoy. Plans for this destination park in Ada County at the corner of Glenwood Avenue and Chinden Boulevard (surrounded by Garden City) were recognized with high honors at the American Planning Association Idaho Conference in Moscow, Idaho earlier this month. Ada County leadership and the design firm PORT received the Outstanding Plan Award for The Park at Expo Idaho. The Outstanding Plan Award recognizes a planning effort that advances the science and art of planning while promoting awareness of its benefits. The award honors excellence in planning through public engagement and effective implementation. We are so proud of Ada County Development Services for shepherding this project from start to finish. While our Development Services Director Richard Beck and Operations Project Manager Josh Brown were the ones to receive the award at the conference, there have been many wonderful people involved in this great project who deserve recognition. From Ada County Procurement Operations, our Legal team, Parks & Waterways and especially Expo Idaho, we are grateful for everyone who has contributed to this project since its inception. County staff and elected officials and especially members of the community have given important input through the public outreach process. We are beyond excited to see the finished product. To learn more about The Park at Expo Idaho, go to https://adacounty.id.gov/commissioners/the- park-at-expo-idaho/ 44

5 ADA COUNTY PROCUREMENT WINS NATIONAL AWARD Achievement of Excellence in Procurement Award from the National Procurement Institute For the fourth year in a row Ada County Procurement has been awarded the prestigious Achievement of Excellence in Procurement (AEP) award from the National Procurement Institute. The AEP Award is earned by agencies that demonstrate a commitment to procurement excellence. This annual program recognizes procurement organizations that embrace Innovation, Professionalism, Productivity, Leadership, and e-Procurement. The AEP program encourages the development of excellence as well as continued organizational improvement to earn the award annually. For 2024, there were 198 successful applicants including 72 cities, 49 counties, 25 special districts, 23 school districts, 16 higher education agencies, and 5 state agencies. Ada County Procurement is the only government agency in Idaho to ever win this award. Pictured Left-Right Olga Tymoshchuk, Buyer Evan Amidan, Procurement Officer II Kathy Corless, Procurement Analyst Alyssa Ellington, Procurement Manager Bob Perkins, Procurement Director Rod Beck, Ada County Commission Chairman Tom Dayley, Ada County Commissioner Ryan Davidson, Ada County Commissioner Robyn Swaney, Procurement Officer II Ken Sinclair, Fleet Manager Learn More about Career Opportunities and Ada County’s Benefits Package https://adacounty.id.gov/human-resources/

TAKING STRIDES TO END DOMESTIC VIOLENCE 6 Thank you to everyone who took part in the “Taking Strides to End Domestic Violence” event Thursday October 3, 2024 in Downtown Boise. October is Domestic Violence Awareness Month - a time to remind anyone experiencing interpersonal violence to reach out for help. Ada County has incredible resources available 24/7. We appreciate the important work being done by the Ada County Prosecutor’s Office, Ada County Victim Services Center, Ada County Sheriff’s Office, Ada County Paramedics, Terry Reilly Health Services, Women’s and Children’s Alliance, and all of our community and health care partners. Domestic violence affects millions of Americans each year with more than three-in-ten women and one-in-ten men experiencing rape, physical violence, and or stalking by a partner. No one should endure this alone. There is great strength in reaching out for help if you think your relationship is causing physical or psychological pain. We are a community that values each and every person and their right to live a life free of physical or emotional abuse. 6

SOLID WASTE TOUR Ada County Commission Chairman Rod Beck and Ada County Landfill Director Herb Cantu hosted Idaho State Senator Lori Den Hartog, Idaho State Senator Ben Adams, and Idaho Association of Counties (IAC) Director of Government Affairs Sara Westbrook for a tour of this state-of-the-art Ada County facility. The Idaho Association of Counties (IAC) is a great organization to know about. IAC is a nonprofit, nonpartisan member service organization. IAC works to improve county government by advocating for good public policy on behalf of all 44 Idaho counties. https://idcounties.org/ DID YOU KNOW? •Our Ada County Landfill does so much more than simply collect trash. We provide Solid Waste Disposal, Household Hazardous Waste & Diversion, and very popular and helpful Education & Outreach Services •We have 50 budgeted employees •Ada County Landfill Operations statistics are impressive: •We collect 1,500 to 2,500 tons of trash a day, •575K Tons a Year •Process 600 – 1,000 Transactions/Day •That’s 1.01 Transactions a Minute Pictured Left-Right Ada County Landfill Director Herb Cantu Ada County Commission Chairman Rod Beck Idaho State Senator Ben Adams Idaho State Senator Lori Den Hartog Idaho Assoc. of Counties Director of Government Affairs Sara Westbrook 7

8 THE MERIDIAN SPEEDWAY – AN ADA COUNTY TREASURE Congratulations to the Meridian Speedway! This popular facility in Ada County sped away with the County Treasure Award this year. The Meridian Speedway has been around since 1951. The motorsport racetrack has a quarter- mile track paved with asphalt and hosts mostly late-model racing, modified racing, and other local- level racing events throughout the year. The Ada County Treasure Award recognizes sites or structures (that must be at least 50 years old) that add to Ada County’s Heritage and are maintained through the dedication of caring individuals, groups, and businesses. The Ada County Historic Preservation Council recognizes the Meridian Dairy Board and the Meridian Speedway for their efforts at preserving Ada County’s Heritage. Ada County Commission Chairman Rod Beck and Ada County Commissioner Ryan Davidson attended the award presentation along with our brilliant staff from Ada County Development Services. Learn more about Ada County Historic Preservation council and see previous winners on our webpage. https://adacounty.id.gov/historicpreservation/ 8

9 ADA COUNTY GOVERNMENT In addition to elected offices, Ada County government includes thirteen individual departments. Each department provides important services to our residents in Star, Eagle, Meridian, Boise, Garden City, Kuna, and Unincorporated Ada County. These services include law enforcement protection, emergency preparedness, election services, parks and waterways, public defense, indigent services, juvenile court, solid waste management, the Western Idaho Fair, Weed, Pest & Mosquito Abatement and more.
